scope: Ninja Golf and transferable guidance for future human-combat games
user_priority_order: Convincing large limb movement, torso rotation, weight transfer, stance and overall posture.
No backwards joints or unnaturally twisted hands and feet.
Cutting edges lead blade travel during an active cut. The blade flat must not lead like a slap.
Refine precise hand and foot contacts after the full-body action reads correctly.
source_motion_lesson: Retain a complete authored or captured body performance, including preparation, step, pelvis/chest turn, balance, impact and recovery. Adapt it to the target rig without replacing it with independent arm targets.
shared_human_constraints: Calibrate anatomical hinge frames and mirrored limbs from the actual rig. Apply the same human movement principles across all characters. Weapon grip, reach and attack style remain specific.
review_method: Review full-speed and slow-motion playback from front, side and three-quarter views. Use numerical tests as supporting evidence, not as a substitute for a convincing overall silhouette.
blade_alignment: Measure cutting-edge and blade-normal alignment with world-space velocity through the meaningful strike interval, not only at one impact frame. Assess thrusts separately using tip travel.
budget_rule: Do not spend long tuning millimetre-scale contacts while the full-body motion remains weak. Reject unsuitable source performances instead of accumulating per-frame corrections.
evidence: Mixamo source performances substantially improved the attacks. A bounded coupled grip fit accepted the Ronin low cut but failed at Ethan's wider polearm grip; source suitability still matters.
